findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil, for example when a mentioned or invited user, or a different logged-in user opening a forwarded email link, has never created a topic_users row for this topic. The next line calls tu.notification_level on nil, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of creating or updating the notification level.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe is performed by an unauthenticated-token GET request
findings.body: The unsubscribe action mutates TopicUser.notification_level on a plain GET and the email link contains no signed token tied to the recipient. Any page, image, mail scanner, or link prefetcher that loads the URL in a logged-in browser will change that session user's notification level without a confirmation or CSRF token, and a forwarded link acts on whoever is logged in rather than the intended recipient.

findings.title: Unsubscribe downgrade is not idempotent, so refreshing changes the level again
findings.body: The action downgrades exactly one step on every GET: watching/tracking (levels 3/2) becomes regular (1), and a subsequent reload of the same unsubscribe URL then turns regular into muted (0). The final state therefore depends on how many times the email link is opened, prefetched, or refreshed, rather than always ending at the intended unsubscribed state.

findings.title: Template name does not match the topicUnsubscribe route
findings.body: The route added in app-route-map.js.es6 is the top-level route topicUnsubscribe, whose route, controller, and view files are all named topic-unsubscribe, so Ember looks for a topic-unsubscribe template. This file is registered as topic/unsubscribe, which corresponds to a nested topic.unsubscribe route that is never defined, so the unsubscribe outlet will not render this template and the page can be blank or raise a missing-template error.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for every add_unsubscribe_link email
findings.body: config/locales/server.en.yml adds %{unsubscribe_url} to the shared unsubscribe_link translation, and both body and html_part interpolate it from template_args, which has no default for unsubscribe_url. Email::MessageBuilder previously allowed add_unsubscribe_link: true by itself (the existing spec did exactly that before being edited here); any such caller or plugin mailer that does not also pass unsubscribe_url will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send.

findings.title: Direct save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
findings.body: set_notifications and other notification-level changes go through TopicUser.change, which sets notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id and publishes a MessageBus notification_level_change. Assigning tu.notification_level and calling save! skips all of that, so open clients keep showing the old watching/tracking state and the change is recorded without the usual reason or timestamp.

findings.title: No tests cover the new unsubscribe endpoint
findings.body: The PR adds a state-changing TopicsController#unsubscribe action but the only spec change adds an unsubscribe_url argument to an existing MessageBuilder example without asserting the URL reaches the body. There is no controller spec exercising level transitions for watching/tracking/regular/muted users, the missing-TopicUser case, slug redirects, or unauthenticated access, so the main regressions in this feature would not be caught.
